input_messages.content: Hello, I’m having a bit of trouble with my phone. It’s been saying “No Service” for the past few hours, and I’m not sure what to do. I mostly use it for calls and texts, so I’m feeling a little lost right now. Can you help me get it working again?
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. Do you need anything else from me?

Oh, I see. So does that mean my phone just won’t work anymore? I’m a bit confused—does this mean I can’t use it for calls or texts at all now? What happens to my photos and everything else on the phone? I really just want to be able to call my family. What do I need to do next?

Oh, I’m relieved my photos are safe! Thank you for explaining that. I do want to be able to call and text again, but I’m not sure what’s best. Could you tell me what my options are for getting a new line or plan? I don’t need anything fancy—just something simple for calls and texts, mostly.

The Basic Plan sounds just right for me—I really don’t use much besides calls and texts. Could you please help me set up a new line with that plan? Will I be able to keep my old phone number, or do I have to get a new one? I get a bit nervous with these things, so I’d appreciate you walking me through what happens next.
Alright, thank you for letting me know. I’ll wait for the next person to help me. I just want to make sure I don’t lose anything important on my phone. Thank you for your patience with me.
Thank you so much for your help and reassurance. I’ll wait for the next agent to help me finish setting things up. I really appreciate your kindness!
Thank you, I appreciate it. Have a wonderful day as well!
Thank you so much! I’ll keep that in mind. Have a lovely day! ###STOP###

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.
